hero_question.reason: The hero shows exactly what Jana asks about — what is left of her salary at the end of each month, answering her complaint that 'at the end of the month there isn't as much left as I expected' with six real months of income versus spending.

about_customer.reason: Every tile is grounded in Jana's actual life — her salary-versus-spending pattern, the monthly repayment to her parents, her emergency fund she is building at 250 a month, her real upcoming bills (Aareblick rent, Bern tax instalment, KPT premium, fitness), and her own card payments at Migros, Coop and Lidl — with nothing generic or belonging to another kind of customer.

titles.reason: All five titles are short, read naturally ('In and out', 'Paying back parents', 'Emergency fund', 'Bills due soon', 'Groceries in November') and accurately name what each tile shows, using terms from her own framing of what's left each month.

not_empty_or_repeated.reason: No tile is empty or zero — the figures (250.82 average left, 150 to her parents, 4'919.20 at 49.2% of the goal, 3'155.45 across six due bills, 1'116.38 groceries) are all real and non-trivial, and no two tiles show the same content since they cover flows, one payee, a savings goal, upcoming obligations and merchant spending respectively.

coherent.reason: The board tells one story under 'What's left': how much of her salary remains each month, the commitments that eat into it (repaying her parents, bills due including her surprise tax instalment), her grocery spend, and the emergency fund she is building — which is exactly the picture of what she can afford that she says she lacks.
